title: A 30-person backyard birthday party on a $400 budget
summary: A fictional party plan that spends $360 and leaves $40 for surprises.

blocks.heading: Feed 30 people. Keep $40 unspent.
blocks.body: Use a two-hour afternoon taco party with water and lemonade, borrowed seating, and a sheet cake. These are planning allowances, not current store prices. Confirm local costs before inviting or buying.

blocks.heading: The $400 envelope
rows: 60 modest taco portions; include beans as a filling
One banner and a simple yard game
Do not spend until headcount and prices are known
blocks.caption: Total $400. Borrowed tables, chairs and indoor backup space are assumptions.

items.label: Confirm 30 attendees
items.detail: Ask about food allergies and dietary needs; label ingredients and keep separate utensils.

items.label: Confirm the rain plan
items.detail: If no indoor space or shelter is available within budget, change the venue or date before buying food.

items.label: Choose food quantity over decorations
items.detail: For a longer event or heartier appetites, add food using the reserve and reduce decorative spending.

blocks.heading: Work backwards from the first guest
items: Two days before: confirm headcount, borrowed equipment and weather alternative.
The day before: shop, label serving dishes, arrange seating and chill drinks.
Before guests arrive: prepare food with clean utensils and safe hot/cold holding; set out small batches and replenish.
After the party: chill perishable leftovers promptly; discard food held unsafely.

blocks.heading: If the estimate rises by $50
blocks.body: Remove $15 of decorations and use $35 of the reserve. If the increase is for equipment instead, simplify the venue before reducing the meal. A $400 plan needs an explicit place for cuts.
